prompt:
Add a `heading_offset` option to `markdown.Markdown` (and `markdown.markdown`): a whole number from 0 to 5, default 0, that shifts the level of every heading Markdown produces by that many (an `h1` becomes an `h2` with 1), never beyond `h6`. Any other value raises `ValueError`.
- It applies to hash and underline headings, and to headings from extensions such as `md_in_html`.
- The `toc` extension sees the shifted levels (its tokens and `toc_depth`).
- The command line gets `--heading-offset N`.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
`heading_offset` (0–5, default 0) is added to `markdown.Markdown` / `markdown.markdown`, and the command line takes `--heading-offset N`; the full test suite passes (1143 tests, 112 skipped — the same 112 as before the change), but flake8 is not installed here so the lint check was not run. The shift is done by a new built-in tree processor that runs before all the others, so `toc` (tokens, `toc_depth`, and `baselevel` applied on top) sees the shifted levels. Behaviours you might not assume: `True`/`False`, `1.0` and `'1'` are rejected with `ValueError`; an out-of-range or non-integer `--heading-offset` exits with a usage error rather than a traceback; plain raw HTML headings (`

…

`) are left as written, but with `md_in_html` both `

` and a raw heading nested inside a `markdown="1"` block are shifted, as `toc`'s `baselevel` already does; a heading that an extension creates in its own tree processor is not shifted. Tests, docs (library, CLI, toc, extension API) and a changelog entry are included.
